evidence.note: Opening exploration follows a sensible read-order (structure → Cargo/lib → model files → tests/runners), showing implicit awareness of where to start, but this is orientation, not a milestone plan tied to test groups.
After surveying scope (137 goldens, ~10K lines), the agent repeatedly frames the task as 'implement things and pass tests' but never breaks it into an ordered set of sub-goals with done-checks.

Shows a flicker of dependency awareness — 'get the foundational types working (Network, Node, Link, basic IO) as those are needed for all tests' — the only genuine sequencing rationale, but it stays a vague intention and is not mapped to specific parity/analysis/CLI test milestones.
Agent abandons after implementing only link.rs/network.rs, submitting the task as complete. No milestone progression was executed; whatever ordering intention existed was not sustained.

reasoning: The agent's exploration had an implicit sensible order and it voiced one dependency insight (foundational model/IO before layout/alignment/CLI), but it never decomposed the port into an ordered set of milestones each with a concrete test-group done-check. The intent stayed at the 'implement things and pass tests' level (anchor 3) with only a thin thread of dependency awareness, and the effort collapsed before any milestone was completed, so it does not reach the component-grouped-with-runnable-checks bar of anchor 5.
